documents.title: Stainless Steel Utensils for Domestic Purposes — Specification
documents.scopeSummary: Covers requirements for domestic stainless steel utensils including water bottles, flasks, tableware, and storage containers manufactured from austenitic and ferritic stainless steel grades.

documents.title: Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)
documents.scopeSummary: Prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for drinking water meant for human consumption, defining acceptable and permissible limits in the absence of alternate sources.

documents.title: Domestic Pressure Cookers — Specification (Fifth Revision)
documents.scopeSummary: Specifies requirements for domestic pressure cookers manufactured from aluminium alloys or stainless steel with operating gauge pressure between 0.5 to 1.1 bar.

documents.title: Safety of Toys — Part 1: Safety Aspects Related to Mechanical and Physical Properties
documents.scopeSummary: Applies to toys intended for use by children under 14 years of age, specifying acceptable criteria for physical characteristics such as sharp edges, points, small parts, and expandability.

documents.title: Protective Helmets for Riders of Two-Wheeler Motor Vehicles — Specification (Fourth Revision)
documents.scopeSummary: Prescribes requirements regarding materials, construction, finish, and testing for protective helmets worn by riders and pillion passengers of two-wheeled motor vehicles.

documents.title: High Strength Deformed Steel Bars and Wires for Concrete Reinforcement — Specification (Fourth Revision)
documents.scopeSummary: Covers technical delivery conditions and requirements for deformed steel bars and wires for use as reinforcement in concrete, grades Fe 415, Fe 415D, Fe 500, Fe 500D, Fe 550, Fe 550D, and Fe 600.

documents.title: Plain and Reinforced Concrete — Code of Practice (Fourth Revision)
documents.scopeSummary: Deals with general structural use of plain and reinforced concrete in buildings and structures, specifying material strengths, water-cement ratios, durability, and limit state design requirements.

qcos.qcoTitle: Stainless Steel and Aluminium Utensils (Quality Control) Order, 2023
qcos.productDescription: Stainless steel utensils including water bottles, flasks, cookware, tableware, and storage containers for domestic use.
qcos.scopeDescription: Goods or articles shall conform to the corresponding Indian Standard IS 14543:2016 and shall bear the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) under a licence from the Bureau of Indian Standards as per Scheme-I of Schedule-II of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018.

qcos.productDescription: Domestic pressure cookers of all capacities and materials (aluminium and stainless steel).
qcos.scopeDescription: Mandates that no person shall manufacture, import, distribute, sell, or offer for sale any domestic pressure cooker unless it conforms to IS 2347:2017 and bears the Standard Mark.

qcos.productDescription: Toys intended for use in play by children under 14 years of age.
qcos.scopeDescription: All toys manufactured or imported into India must strictly conform to IS 9873 (Parts 1-9) and bear the Standard Mark under Scheme-I.

qcos.qcoTitle: Helmets for riders of Two Wheeler Motor Vehicles (Quality Control) Order, 2020
qcos.productDescription: Protective helmets for drivers and pillion riders of two-wheeled motor vehicles.
qcos.scopeDescription: Mandatory conformity to IS 4151:2015 with ISI certification mark. Non-ISI helmets are illegal for sale in India under the Motor Vehicles Act.

qcos.qcoTitle: Steel and Steel Products (Quality Control) Order, 2020
qcos.productDescription: High strength deformed steel bars and wires (TMT rebar) for concrete reinforcement.
qcos.scopeDescription: Prohibits manufacture, import, sale, or distribution of TMT steel bars without BIS certification mark under IS 1786.

chunks.content: This standard prescribes the requirements, materials, and test methods for stainless steel utensils intended for domestic purposes, including drinking water bottles, flasks, cookware, serving vessels, and dinnerware. It covers utensils manufactured from wrought, sheet, or strip stainless steel complying with recognized food-contact grades.
chunks.contentWithContext:
[IS 14543:2016 | Clause 1 | Scope]
This standard prescribes the requirements, materials, and test methods for stainless steel utensils intended for domestic purposes, including drinking water bottles, flasks, cookware, serving vessels, and dinnerware. It covers utensils manufactured from wrought, sheet, or strip stainless steel complying with recognized food-contact grades.

chunks.content: Stainless steel utensils including water bottles coming into direct contact with food or potable water shall be manufactured from austenitic stainless steel of Designation Grade 304 (equivalent to X04Cr19Ni9 conforming to IS 6911) or Grade 316. Ferritic stainless steel grades (such as Grade 430) may only be used for external cladding or non-food contact surfaces. Re-melted scrap or uncertified stainless steel alloys shall not be utilized.
chunks.contentWithContext:
[IS 14543:2016 | Clause 4.1 | Material Requirements]
Stainless steel utensils including water bottles coming into direct contact with food or potable water shall be manufactured from austenitic stainless steel of Designation Grade 304 (equivalent to X04Cr19Ni9 conforming to IS 6911) or Grade 316. Ferritic stainless steel grades (such as Grade 430) may only be used for external cladding or non-food contact surfaces. Re-melted scrap or uncertified stainless steel alloys shall not be utilized.

chunks.content:
When tested in accordance with IS 228 (relevant parts), the chemical composition of Grade 304 stainless steel used for water bottles and utensils shall comply with the following mandatory limits: Chromium (Cr): 17.50 to 19.50 percent by mass; Nickel (Ni): 8.00 to 10.50 percent by mass; Carbon (C): 0.08 percent max; Manganese (Mn): 2.00 percent max; Silicon (Si): 0.75 percent max; Sulfur (S): 0.030 percent max; Phosphorus (P): 0.045 percent max.

Table 1 Mandatory Chemical Composition for Grade 304 Stainless Steel:
| Constituent Element | Chemical Symbol | Mandatory Limit (% by mass) |
|---|---|---|
| Chromium | Cr | 17.50 to 19.50 |
| Nickel | Ni | 8.00 to 10.50 |
| Carbon | C | 0.08 max |
| Manganese | Mn | 2.00 max |
| Silicon | Si | 0.75 max |
| Sulfur | S | 0.030 max |
| Phosphorus | P | 0.045 max |

chunks.content: Utensils and bottles shall be subjected to the boiling citric acid test. The sample shall be immersed in a boiling aqueous solution containing 3 percent (w/v) citric acid for a duration of two hours. After the test, the surface of the article shall show no visual signs of corrosion, pitting, discoloration, etching, or breakdown of the protective passivated chromium oxide layer.
chunks.contentWithContext:
[IS 14543:2016 | Clause 5.1 | Corrosion Resistance Test]
Utensils and bottles shall be subjected to the boiling citric acid test. The sample shall be immersed in a boiling aqueous solution containing 3 percent (w/v) citric acid for a duration of two hours. After the test, the surface of the article shall show no visual signs of corrosion, pitting, discoloration, etching, or breakdown of the protective passivated chromium oxide layer.

chunks.content: Each stainless steel utensil or water bottle shall be legibly and indelibly stamped or etched on the base with: (a) Manufacturer name or recognized trademark, (b) Grade of stainless steel (e.g., 304 or 316), (c) Nominal volume capacity in millilitres or litres, and (d) The Standard Mark (ISI Mark) together with the license number (CM/L-XXXXXXXXXX). Under the Stainless Steel Utensils QCO, 2023, sale without the ISI mark is prohibited by law.

chunks.content:
Every domestic pressure cooker shall be fitted with at least two independent safety relief devices in addition to the primary weight valve/pressure regulator: (a) A safety valve or secondary relief valve designed to operate between 1.4 to 1.8 times the normal working pressure (maximum 2.0 bar) should the vent tube become blocked, and (b) A fusible plug or metallic gasket release system (GMR) which releases excess pressure before the internal pressure reaches 3.0 times the rated design pressure.

Table 1 Pressure Cooker Safety Relief Devices Operating Parameters:
| Safety Device Type | Operating Pressure Threshold | Functional Safety Role |
|---|---|---|
| Primary Weight Valve / Regulator | 1.0× Normal Operating Pressure | Continuous operational regulation |
| Secondary Safety Relief Valve | 1.4× to 1.8× Operating Pressure (Max 2.0 bar) | Vent tube blockage relief |
| Fusible Plug / GMR Gasket Release | Before 3.0× Rated Design Pressure | Ultimate overpressure release |
chunks.contentWithContext:

chunks.clauseTitle: Hydrostatic Proof and Burst Pressure Test
chunks.content: The cooker body and lid assembly shall withstand internal hydrostatic pressure of not less than 2.0 times the nominal operating pressure for a continuous duration of 5 minutes without showing any permanent distortion, leakage, or rupture. In hydrostatic burst pressure testing, the vessel shall not rupture at a pressure lower than 3.0 times the declared normal working pressure.
chunks.contentWithContext:
[IS 2347:2017 | Clause 5.2 | Hydrostatic Proof and Burst Pressure Test]

In hydrostatic burst pressure testing, the vessel shall not rupture at a pressure lower than 3.0 times the declared normal working pressure.

chunks.clauseTitle: Mandatory Certification and Verification for Consumers
chunks.content: Under the Domestic Pressure Cookers (Quality Control) Order, 2020 issued by DPIIT, all pressure cookers sold in India must mandatorily bear the ISI Mark. Consumers can verify genuine certification by locating the 7 or 8-digit CML license number under the ISI monogram and verifying it using the official BIS Care mobile application or the BIS online directory (services.bis.gov.in).
chunks.contentWithContext:
[IS 2347:2017 | Clause 8.1 | Mandatory Certification and Verification for Consumers]

Consumers can verify genuine certification by locating the 7 or 8-digit CML license number under the ISI monogram and verifying it using the official BIS Care mobile application or the BIS online directory (services.bis.gov.in).

chunks.content: Toys intended for children under 36 months of age, and toys or components detachable from them, shall not fit entirely within the small parts test cylinder (dimensions 31.7 mm diameter and 25.4 mm to 57.1 mm truncated oblique cylinder) when subjected to normal use or abuse testing (drop test, torque test, tension test of 90 N). Compliance with this clause is mandatory under the Toys (Quality Control) Order, 2020.

Compliance with this clause is mandatory under the Toys (Quality Control) Order, 2020.

chunks.content: Accessible edges, points, and corners on all toys intended for children under 14 years shall not present an unreasonable risk of injury. Accessible metal or glass edges shall be rolled, hemmed, curled, or covered with protective coatings. Test methods for sharpness of edges shall be performed according to Clause 8.11 using the sharp edge tester.

chunks.clauseTitle: Materials and Construction for Two-Wheeler Helmets
chunks.content: Helmets for two-wheeler motor vehicle riders shall consist of: (1) An outer hard protective shell composed of impact-resistant thermoplastic (such as ABS or Polycarbonate) or reinforced fiber resin; (2) An energy-absorbing impact liner made of high-density expanded polystyrene (EPS); (3) Internal comfort padding; and (4) A retention system with chin strap.
chunks.contentWithContext:
[IS 4151:2015 | Clause 4.1 | Materials and Construction for Two-Wheeler Helmets]
Helmets for two-wheeler motor vehicle riders shall consist of: (1) An outer hard protective shell composed of impact-resistant thermoplastic (such as ABS or Polycarbonate) or reinforced fiber resin; (2) An energy-absorbing impact liner made of high-density expanded polystyrene (EPS); (3) Internal comfort padding; and (4) A retention system with chin strap.

chunks.clauseTitle: Retention System and Chin Strap Requirements
chunks.content: The chin strap of the retention system shall have a minimum width of 20 mm under a tensile load of 150 N. The fastening device (micrometric buckle or double D-ring) shall not be capable of opening inadvertently under dynamic load. Dynamic displacement of the retention system shall not exceed 35 mm when tested with a falling mass of 10 kg.

[IS 4151:2015 | Clause 5.2 | Retention System and Chin Strap Requirements]

chunks.clauseTitle: Cement and Water Requirements in Concrete
chunks.content: The cement used shall conform to IS 269 (33 grade OPC), IS 8112 (43 grade OPC), IS 12269 (53 grade OPC), or IS 455 (PSC). Water used for mixing and curing shall be clean and free from injurious amounts of oils, acids, alkalis, salts, and organic materials. Potable water conforming to IS 10500 is generally considered satisfactory for mixing concrete.
chunks.contentWithContext:
[IS 456:2000 | Clause 5.1 | Cement and Water Requirements in Concrete]

Water used for mixing and curing shall be clean and free from injurious amounts of oils, acids, alkalis, salts, and organic materials. Potable water conforming to IS 10500 is generally considered satisfactory for mixing concrete.
